title: Actuals
description: What was ACTUALLY spent in one month, reconciled from bank statements — one file per month, named for the month it covers (data/actuals/2026-08.json). Display only: nothing here feeds Balance, Available to spend, Total private expenses or the account roll-forward, all of which stay planned-based. Every transaction carries exactly one of category, ignored or untracked, so the file accounts for every row on the statement and both 'deliberately skipped' and 'not decided yet' are recorded rather than inferred from absence. coverage is what stops a mid-month import reading as a spectacular underspend.

month.description: The month this file covers, YYYY-MM. Must match the filename — a mismatch means an import was saved over the wrong month.

coverage.description: Which account was read, and through which dates. Never empty: 'nothing imported yet' is the absent file, not an empty one. Until coverage spans the whole month the dashboard withholds any under-budget judgement, since on the 5th every category is trivially under.

account.description: The account this range was read from, spelled as the transactions spell it.

from.description: First day read, inclusive. Must fall inside month.

to.description: Last day read, inclusive. Must fall inside month and not precede from.

imported_at.description: When the statement was read. Informational — only from/to affect any figure.

id.description: Stable within this file, so re-uploading the same statement is idempotent rather than duplicating every line. Derived deterministically from account+date+amount+description, with a -2 suffix on collision.

date.description: Must fall inside month: a statement spanning a month boundary splits into two files.

description.description: The statement line as the bank wrote it. Admin-only — it never reaches a non-admin session's HTML, and only the spending detail page renders it.

amount.description: Euros, decimals allowed. Positive = money out, matching budget.json's convention; a refund is a negative amount against the same category. Never 0 — a zero line is noise, and 'saw it, not an expense' is what ignored is for.

account.description: Which account it was charged to. Free text, and deliberately not checked against accounts.json: that file lists the accounts whose balance is carried, which is not the same set as the cards and accounts a statement line can arrive on.

category.description: The budget category id this line belongs to. Exactly one of category, ignored, untracked or splits must be set — that rule is enforced in Go, since expressing it here would generate poor code. A category that no longer resolves fails validation loudly rather than silently dropping the money.

ignored.description: Why this line is not a budget expense — 'salary', 'transfer to savings'. A non-empty reason, never a bare true: the file is meant to reconcile line-for-line against the statement, and the spending page lists these so a mis-ignored line is visible. Excluded from every figure.

untracked.description: Why this line has not been decided yet — 'ATM withdrawal, cash not spent yet'. Money that left the account and belongs to no category so far, which is what cash mostly is until you remember what it went on. A note rather than a bare true, for the same reason ignored is: a line parked here for two months should say what it is waiting on. Different from ignored, which is a decision that this is not a budget expense; this one is the decision to decide later, and the spending page lists it prominently and marks the month so it does not sit here forever. Excluded from every figure while it does — untracked money is spent but unattributed, and counting it against a plan would misstate both.

splits.description: Set instead of category, ignored or untracked when one statement line paid for more than one thing. The line itself stays a single row so the file still reconciles line-for-line against the statement; the parts must add up to its amount. Two or more parts — one part is just a category.

movement.description: What this line moved between the company and its owner, set ALONGSIDE ignored rather than instead of it — such a line genuinely is not a budget expense, so it still carries a reason like every other ignored line. It is what the director's loan is settled from. The first four cross between the two of you and move that balance: salary_transfer, owner_draw and dividend_payout hand money to the owner, owner_contribution puts money back in. The last two leave the company for the state and move nothing; they are marked only so the spending page can list them rather than burying them among the ignored lines. RECORD IT ONCE, ON THE COMPANY STATEMENT: both statements are imported, so the same transfer arrives twice, and counting it twice is the one way this figure goes quietly wrong. The sign enforces it — everything except owner_contribution must be money OUT of the company (a positive amount) and owner_contribution must be money in (negative), so the mirror line on the private statement, whose sign is the other way round, cannot be marked at all.

split.description: One part of a statement line that paid for more than one thing — a 100 EUR cash withdrawal that was 50 of cleaning and 50 of restaurant. A part carries exactly one of category, ignored or untracked, the same rule a whole line follows.

amount.description: Euros, same sign convention as the line it belongs to. Never 0, and the parts must add up to the line's own amount — a split that does not reconcile to the statement is worse than no split.

category.description: The budget category id this part belongs to. Exactly one of category, ignored or untracked, enforced in Go for the same reason as on the line itself.

ignored.description: Why this part is not a budget expense — 'moved to savings'. Lets a withdrawal that was partly spent and partly moved to your own account be recorded as what it was.

untracked.description: Why this part is not decided yet — 'the rest is still in my wallet'. The case a split exists for: 100 out of the machine, 60 of it recognisably groceries and 40 still unaccounted for, recorded as exactly that instead of guessing at the 40 or ignoring the whole line.
